reviews.review:
[b]Warframe[/b] is a game that can either be loved to the point you play hundreds to thousands of hours in a very short amount of time, or be remarkably disliked.

It can be understandable in terms of why someone would dislike playing [i]Warframe[/i] when it comes to the grinding aspect of the game, sometimes it can be very frustrating how many times you have to repeat the same mission over and over to get that one part, that one item. However, there are also players like me whom do find satisfaction in grinding that much, hence Warframe is definitely not for those who have no patience nor pleasure in (excuse the term) working hard to get what you want.

Some might say that [i]Warframe[/i] runs a pay-to-win model, looking at the shop, but when we take a deeper look at it there is no actual basis to definite it so. Everything you buy with real-life currency can be obtained without - except, of course, some cosmetic items. Most of what you can purchase with Platinum you can buy with in-game credits too, hence the advantage that Platinum provides is simply getting things done faster.

[i]Warframe[/i] unleashes an incredibly high level of optimization! Sure, it requires a good machine in order to run it at high settings, but it is very light and is very, very well optimized. The graphics are stunning, the level of details is incredible. Overall it certainly is a masterpiece to whom, like me, loves playing games with this kind of graphics.

In terms of gameplay and mechanics, I do love the combat system - I'm not exaggerating when I say that it has one of the best movements and combat I've ever had the pleasure to play with. What makes the game very sustainable in a long-term stay is the amount of different 'characters', weapons, missions, bosses and modes Warframe has to offer.

I highly suggest you give [i]Warframe[/i] a try - it is free, afterall.
This game should not be free. It is too good to be a free game
